document_title: Investigator evidence and case writing guide
text: Write the authorisation facts first, unknowns second, and later findings in a separate dated section. Preserve the source transaction and document identifier. A decline is not a fraud label. A dispute is not necessarily an unauthorised payment. The synthetic verdict is known sixty days after the transaction. Human review is required to turn generated candidates into gold investigation examples.

document_title: PII handling and synthetic identifier guide
text: The generator creates no names, addresses, phones, card numbers or payment handles. C, M and D identifiers are reproducible random-looking tokens, not hashes of real people. Monetary values and cities are fictional event attributes. Review a deterministic sample of one thousand documents using identifier detectors, and separately test any real corpus with an approved recogniser and a human audit. A regex pass is not a proof that arbitrary text is PII-free.

document_title: Training splits and label availability guide
text: Authorisations from January through October 2025 form the retrospective training split. November and December 2025 form validation. January and February 2026 are holdout. All labels are mature at the May 2026 snapshot. Retrospective splitting does not recreate a model deployed on November first: use eligible_at_next_split_start for that stricter backtest. CPT candidates also require a publication date before November first. MCC encoding uses earlier training labels already mature at the frozen month boundary.

document_title: Supabase synthetic environment guide
text: Load into a dedicated PostgreSQL schema using COPY over an encrypted direct or session-pooler connection. Dataset tables have RLS enabled and no anonymous or authenticated policy. Use private Storage buckets and service-side credentials. Keep a separate evaluation bucket for holdout artifacts. A private Supabase bucket does not implement the AWS Object Lock requirement in the production design. The hosted dataset is a teaching environment; the production architecture remains a separate client decision.

document_title: Risk based approach teaching guide
text: Risk assessment combines amount, account tenure, observed device and city changes, failed outcomes and velocity. Inherent contextual risk is distinct from residual risk after a documented verification control. Record likelihood, impact, evidence confidence, mitigating controls and the reason for escalation. This data factory does not conduct KYC, AML screening or a legal RBA assessment. Use the known fraud targets only after prediction when assessing model quality. The fraud score simulator is uncalibrated and cannot establish production cutoffs.

text:
Investigation procedure:
First confirm the transaction reference and feature timestamp. Then list observed facts, identify unknown fields and compare alternative legitimate explanations. Inspect only the history available before authorisation. Record later dispute evidence separately. Escalate combinations of signals according to the active policy and record why an action was selected.

document_title: Synthetic RBI topic exercise 0799 on access review
text:
Teaching policy:
The project starts with probability cutoffs 0.30, 0.60 and 0.85. Below 0.60 the policy allows the payment; from 0.60 to below 0.85 it requests review; at or above 0.85 it blocks. A blocklisted device takes precedence over a customer allowlist. These are client-provided starting settings, not a regulatory standard.
